data.narrative:
Hybron is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Brennan Lieu and Aaron Guo that has raised $30M to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the peer set remains narrow within this early-stage, capital-intensive sector.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-Progression analysis uses the $30M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding a $75M implied valuation. Peer-Median analysis was not viable; while 10 same-sector robotics companies exist in the comparable universe, fewer than three datapoints met the filtering criteria of same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. A broader sectoral median would introduce unacceptable noise given heterogeneity in robotics subsectors and funding trajectories.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $64M–$86M, centered at $75M. This narrow, single-method triangulation reflects structural constraints in comparable availability rather than conviction. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x step-up multiplier for this specific subsector, capital efficiency relative to peers, and technology differentiation. Any refined valuation should await either (i) a tighter peer cohort or (ii) additional financial metrics on Hybron's unit economics and burn rate.
